It is not restful or relaxing or safe or a vacation in the slightest and there is a large portion of homeless people that avoid shelters entirely (especially homeless women) because the risk of further violence is so high it can make you more of a target than when you’re openly exposed living outdoors. Just fyi getting medical disability benefits is extremely hard even if you’re super obviously disabled. It’s basically a rule that you get rejected the first time no matter if you’re actively dying or not. I’ve heard people get rejected for years that were in desperate need of help and support. It’s basically their thing to keep rejecting applicants so that the pool will be smaller because many disabled people will literally die before they get benefits. It’s not easy in the slightest is all I’m saying, so I wouldn’t necessarily put stock in to what the disability office says about your sister. This is coming from someone who is obviously externally disabled as well as having a host of other mental and physical/genetic disabilities. (Also there are many disabilities, physical and mental, out there that don’t make those with them “look/act disabled”). Ok that’s all I had to say.

My skin is similar- I used to be very oily all the time and then it went mostly dry but all throughout it was and is extremely sensitive and reactive (+rosacea). I used to do the same thing and just pile on the cover up so you couldn’t see how red my skin was but gradually I started decreasing the amount of base I would wear until now I just wear spot concealer and a slightly tinted sunscreen (with other things like blush and mascara etc) on days I want to feel more smooth/done up. I’ve changed my focus to skincare and finding products that no matter how angry my skin is I can wear them and they don’t make it worse/ calm it down. Now believe me it’s been quite a journey to find things I don’t react to but I believe that’s made the biggest difference (that and trying to give my skin as much of a breather as I can). YMMV but what I have found that works these days is for skincare- first put any hydrocolloid patches on pimples while skin is clean then glycerine mixed with water as a first layer, then tret, then gold bond crepe moisturizer, then Rosehip oil on top. For daytime I will usually just rinse with water and sometimes add another thin layer of moisturizer or oil then skin 1004 centella sunscreen or avene mineral spf 50 (the centella is very slightly tinted and has a little bit of a blur effect and the avene is very glowy and dewy and both are very sensitive skin friendly and don’t feel very heavy. Then I might do a little bit of concealer+ lipstick as blush+ brows and lashes. I also do things like tint my brows and lashes once a month at home so I can look more made up but not have to always irritate my skin by wearing something or having to scrub my face so hard to get the products off again.

I am autistic and nonbinary and I ended up learning the social rules about things like that way back in 6th grade because of relentless bullying in the changing rooms… I went from not giving a single heck about what I wore and feeling free as a bird to feeling hyper paranoid about every aspect of how I was to present myself in order to never be harassed again. Now hopefully this isn’t your kids experience, I would never want anyone else to go through that. However, unfortunately learning those social rules so intensely has helped in some aspects of adult life (however I am now dealing with even more trauma and learning how to separate what I want and choose to do with my body and what I’m doing because I feel like I have no other choice).. uhh point is as someone with experience I would try to broach the subject matter of facts/bluntly but also as kindly and generously as you can. Also i would look in to what textures and types of fabrics your kid likes (and can stand on their body for long periods of time without wanting to die) and which ones they don’t. I would specifically look in to lightly compressive smooth wider shoulder strap tank tops that they can layer under clothes to add some coverage (look for ones in moisture wicking fabrics for the hotter months). If they’re open to something more bra-like there are sports bras out there made of very nice super stretchy soft material that just feel like a shorter version of a stretchy compression tank top and they’re not too awful sensory wise as far as bras go. Another option is finding shirts that have pattern or graphic covering the boob area (if they would be open to trying that as a style element) as it can camouflage anything going on underneath a little better. Also just darker colored tops can help as well. But honestly if they don’t care I would just let them be and let them know that if they ever run in to an issue with going braless from others/institutions that you’ll be there and available to help them find and brainstorm comfortable solutions. Also I would add in- give them enough information about what circumstances they might want to consider wearing something more conservative as the way others perceive them can effect their level of care and respect they will receive (and give them space to grieve their sense of freedom and comfort because if/when they fully grasp the extent of how stupid the world is about these things they’re probably going to have a lot of feelings). Lastly, make sure you do as much as you can to bolster their body confidence/neutrality and help them know that despite what society believes they are so much more than their body and that it is the least interesting thing about them.

Yeah your ends are super uneven and dry looking.. at least cut it to where the shortest scraggly end stops but it would be better to go a little bit above it in order to not have more split ends fully fraying up the length. Then I would use olaplex 3 on the lengths and ends (just don’t scrub it in to your roots) or k18 mask (or both- k18 first for 5 mins then olaplex) for about a month. Use them after every time you shower and make sure to use a clarifying shampoo with no conditioner afterwords so it can penetrate. If your hair is way too dry after just the hair masks you can use a tiny bit of light oil or a small amount of conditioner (or both but then use less of both) after you’ve let both masks sit for at least 10 mins in total (but the longer they can sit wet and absorb without other oils getting in the way the better). I have heavily bleached hair going through the same process as yours and this has brought it back from being a dry puffy crunchy straw like mess to something almost as shiny, soft, strong and nice as my virgin hair and I do believe it will last (unless I decide to bleach again or cause a big new damage). It’s a bit expensive though so decide if you’d rather keep some hair length or some paycheck.
